title: Smooth and allowed coefficients
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the notion of smooth morphism of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Equivalently, by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], $f$ is smooth if and only if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is smooth over its residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The fibres need not be varieties of finite type.

Let $S,T$ be schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] has allowed torsion with respect to $S$ if, for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and every element $x$ of the geometric stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], there is a positive integer $d$ with $dx=0$ and $d\cdot1$ a unit of $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. Invertibility is global on $S$; no common annihilator is required.

For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the projection $\mathbf A^n_S\to S$ of [def-sbc-affine-space] is smooth. The global allowed-torsion condition is stronger than requiring each stalk element to have an annihilator invertible on a neighbourhood of its underlying point when $T=S$: on $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the sheaf $j_!\underline{\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z}$, for the open immersion $j:D(2)\hookrightarrow S$ [def-weil-open-immersion], has the latter property but not the former. Here the underlined sheaf is constant [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $j_!$ is extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero].

Put $I_S=\{d\in\mathbb N: d>0,\ d\cdot1\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)^\times\}$, ordered by divisibility. For $d\in I_S$, define the $\Lambda$-module subsheaf $\mathcal F[d]$ by $\mathcal F[d](U)=\{s\in\mathcal F(U):ds=0\}$, with the restrictions of $\mathcal F$; its underlying abelian sheaf is $\ker(d:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]. For $d\mid e$, use the inclusion $\mathcal F[d]\hookrightarrow\mathcal F[e]$. If $\mathcal F$ has allowed torsion with respect to $S$, these form a small filtered diagram and the canonical morphism
$$c:\varinjlim_{d\in I_S}\mathcal F[d]\longrightarrow\mathcal F$$
is an isomorphism in the category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$; this is the asserted filtered union [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: The smoothness terminology is that of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] to the arbitrary morphism $f:X\to Y$: its stated equivalence is exactly flatness, local finite presentation, and smoothness of every residue-field fibre, with no quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis. This proves the characterization written above and avoids interpreting “variety” as an extra finiteness or irreducibility condition.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], for every scheme $S$ and $n\geq0$ the affine-space projection is smooth of relative dimension $n$. By the definition in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], smooth of relative dimension $n$ includes smoothness. Hence the projection is smooth, including $n=0$.

source.place: paragraph 2, affine-space projection sentence; existing affine-space lemma

proof.text: The subsheaf $\mathcal F[d]$ is closed under addition, negatives, and the $\Lambda$-action because $d(a s)=a(ds)$, and the condition $ds=0$ glues uniquely by the sheaf axiom. Its abelian kernel and sectionwise description are [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]; the module forgetful functor preserves these kernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. If $d\mid e$, write $e=kd$; then $ds=0$ implies $es=k(ds)=0$, giving the stated inclusions and their composition laws. The set $I_S$ is nonempty because $1$ is a global unit, and $d,e\in I_S$ have common upper bound $de\in I_S$, since $(de)^{-1}=e^{-1}d^{-1}$ in the global-section ring. A preordered set has at most one arrow between two objects, so no parallel-arrow condition remains: it is a small filtered category. The module colimit $L$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The compatible inclusions $i_d:\mathcal F[d]\to\mathcal F$ induce $c:L\to\mathcal F$ with $c\iota_d=i_d$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); agent argument for the globally invertible divisibility diagram

proof.text: Forget the $\Lambda$-action; by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], the underlying abelian sheaf of $L$ is the colimit of the underlying abelian diagram. The inclusions $i_d$ constructed in the preceding step are monic, so they give an objectwise monic natural transformation to the constant diagram with value $\mathcal F$. Exactness of filtered colimits in [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck] makes its colimit monic. The colimit of the constant diagram is $\mathcal F$: any cocone has equal components, since any two indices map into their product, and its common component is its unique factorization. Thus that colimit morphism is precisely the underlying map $c$, which is monic.

Let $\bar t$ be any geometric point and $x\in\mathcal F_{\bar t}$. Allowed torsion supplies $d\in I_S$ with $dx=0$. Exactness of the abelian geometric-stalk functor [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies $(\mathcal F[d])_{\bar t}$ with $\ker(d:\mathcal F_{\bar t}\to\mathcal F_{\bar t})$, so $x$ lifts to some $y$ in this stalk. Then $(\iota_d)_{\bar t}(y)\in L_{\bar t}$ maps to $x$ under $c_{\bar t}$ because $c\iota_d=i_d$. Thus every $c_{\bar t}$ is surjective. It is also injective, since the exact stalk functor preserves the monomorphism from the preceding step. The underlying abelian map $c$ is therefore an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Its inverse is $\Lambda$-linear: for a local section $z$, the two sections $c^{-1}(a z)$ and $a c^{-1}(z)$ have equal images under the injective $c$, namely $a z$. Hence $c$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves. This proves the actual restricted union, without assuming that $I_S$ is cofinal in all positive integers.

For the comparison example put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, $U=D(2)$, and $G=j_!\underline{\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the constant sheaf has stalk $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ at every geometric point of $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], $G$ has those stalks on $U$ and zero stalks on the complement. On $U$, the integer $2$ kills every stalk and is a unit on the open neighbourhood $D(2)$; at points outside $U$ the zero stalk is killed by the unit $1$. But a nonzero stalk element on $U$ cannot be killed by a positive integer globally invertible on $S$: the global-section ring is $\mathbb Z$, whose only positive unit is $1$, and $1$ does not kill the nonzero element of $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. This proves the distinction claimed in the statement.
